title: Connection Pool Packet Reassembler Repair
scenario: A database administrator is investigating a post-incident outage. The internal tooling team wrote a small Python codebase (~1,400 lines) that proxies connections to a PostgreSQL replica pool, logs all query packets to a binary rolling log, and has a reassembler service that reconstructs multi-fragment query sessions from those logs for forensic replay. After a partial failover last night, the reassembler started producing garbled session replays; the DBA needs the replay output to be byte-for-byte identical to what the live replica actually executed, so they can audit which queries ran. The codebase has a running log emitter (a compiled C extension, no source in the repo) that produces the binary log, a broken Python reassembler that the DBA must diagnose and repair, and a reference replay validator that the DBA must also implement from scratch.
instruction_draft:
```
$ python3 replay_validator.py --session-log /var/log/pgproxy/sessions.binlog --output /tmp/replay.sql
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "replay_validator.py", line 11, in <module>
    from reassembler import SessionReassembler
ImportError: cannot import name 'SessionReassembler' from 'reassembler'

$ python3 -c "import log_emitter; log_emitter.emit_test_session('/tmp/t.binlog')"
[emitter] wrote 47 fragments across 3 sessions to /tmp/t.binlog

$ python3 reassembler.py /tmp/t.binlog
Session 1: 2 queries recovered
Session 2: 0 queries recovered   <-- should be 3
Session 3: 1 queries recovered   <-- should be 2
```

The DBA left this note: "After the failover, some sessions span log-file boundary segments (the emitter rotates files mid-session and the fragment stream can arrive out-of-order by up to the configured reorder_window). The reassembler never handled this correctly — it was masked because pre-incident traffic was too light to trigger cross-file sessions or reorder. Fix the reassembler so that every session's queries are recovered completely and in execution order. Then implement the missing `SessionReassembler` class that `replay_validator.py` imports, so the validator produces a valid SQL replay file.

Requirements:
1. `python3 reassembler.py <binlog>` must recover every query in every session in the correct execution order for any single log file.
2. `python3 reassembler.py --merge <dir>` must correctly reassemble sessions that span multiple rotated log files in the directory, handling fragments delivered out of order within the configured `reorder_window`.
3. The `SessionReassembler` class exported from `reassembler.py` must accept a list of log file paths, reassemble all sessions, and expose a `sessions` dict mapping session_id to an ordered list of query byte strings.
4. `python3 replay_validator.py --session-log <binlog_dir> --output <file>` must write a valid SQL replay: each session's queries in order, separated by a session header comment, with sessions ordered by their first query's global sequence number.
5. The reassembler must correctly handle: fragments arriving out-of-order within the reorder window, sessions split across log file rotation boundaries, and fragment deduplication (the emitter may re-emit the last fragment of a file at the start of the next file as a continuity marker).
requirements: reassembler.py single-file mode recovers every query in every session in correct execution order
reassembler.py --merge <dir> mode handles sessions spanning multiple rotated log files
reassembler.py --merge handles fragments delivered out of order within the configured reorder_window
SessionReassembler class is importable from reassembler and exposes sessions dict mapping session_id to ordered list of query bytestrings
replay_validator.py produces valid SQL replay with sessions ordered by first query's global sequence number
Reassembler correctly deduplicates continuity-marker fragments that appear at both the end of one log file and the start of the next
Reassembler correctly handles the reorder_window parameter from the proxy config file
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm; installs: build-essential, libpq-dev, sqlite3

Compiled C extension /app/lib/log_emitter.so (built from hidden source during Docker build, installed as importable log_emitter); exports emit_test_session(path), emit_stress_session(path, seed, n_sessions, n_files) — no source in image

Binary log format: each fragment is a 32-byte header (magic 4B, session_id 4B uint32, frag_seq 4B uint32, global_seq 8B uint64, payload_len 4B uint32, flags 4B: bit0=first, bit1=last, bit2=continuation_dup, reserved 8B) followed by payload bytes; a session's query boundaries are encoded as null-byte delimiters within the assembled payload
/app/proxy_config.ini with [pool] section containing reorder_window=8 and log_rotation_bytes=1048576

/app/reassembler.py: ~350 lines, broken — correctly parses single-file single-session cases, but: (a) ignores frag_seq ordering, naively appends in read order; (b) has no cross-file merging logic; (c) does not deduplicate continuation_dup fragments; (d) SessionReassembler class stub raises NotImplementedError
/app/replay_validator.py: ~120 lines, imports SessionReassembler, calls it, formats output — complete except for the missing class
/app/schema/fragment_format.md: precise binary format documentation including all header fields, flag definitions, the null-byte query delimiter convention, and the continuation_dup semantics
/app/tests/: directory with sample .binlog files covering simple single-session cases only (the cross-file and reorder cases are absent from samples)
/var/log/pgproxy/: directory with a pre-generated multi-file log set (sessions.d/) produced by the emitter at build time using a fixed seed, demonstrating the broken behavior

At verify time, tests call log_emitter.emit_stress_session() with fresh seeds to generate new log sets and compare reassembler output against the emitter's own ground-truth session manifest (also returned by emit_stress_session)
internal_hint: Difficulty source 1 (observe_not_read): The reassembler's bugs only manifest with cross-file sessions and out-of-order fragments — the test data in /app/tests/ never triggers them, and reading the reassembler code shows logic that looks plausible for the simple case. The solver must run the emitter against the pre-generated logs in /var/log/pgproxy/ to see the wrong output, read the fragment_format.md to understand the binary protocol fully (especially continuation_dup and frag_seq ordering), and instrument the reassembler to observe the actual fragment stream. Difficulty source 2 (build_component): SessionReassembler is a non-trivial class that must: parse binary headers with struct.unpack, sort fragments by frag_seq within session within file, merge across files by matching session_id and continuing frag_seq ranges, deduplicate continuation_dup-flagged fragments (bit2 set means 'I am a copy of the last fragment of the previous file — skip me if you've already seen this frag_seq for this session'), split assembled payloads on null bytes to recover individual queries, and respect reorder_window from proxy_config.ini by buffering out-of-order fragments up to that many positions before flushing. A solver who only reads the broken code and patches the obvious parts (adding a sort by frag_seq) will pass the simple tests but fail on: cross-file sessions (no cross-file tracking), continuation_dup deduplication (will double-count that query), reorder_window buffering (will emit queries too early or too late on stressed inputs).
trap: A solver who sorts fragments by frag_seq within a single file passes the provided sample tests. The hidden tests use emit_stress_session with fresh seeds that generate: (1) sessions whose fragment streams span 3+ log files, (2) fragment sequences with gaps up to reorder_window-1 that must be buffered before flushing, (3) continuation_dup fragments that if not deduplicated corrupt the query boundary detection causing downstream queries to be split wrong. Any of these three failures causes query-level mismatches against the ground truth manifest.
tests: Single-file correctness: emit_stress_session(seed=X, n_sessions=5, n_files=1), run reassembler.py on output, compare recovered query lists to ground-truth manifest returned by emitter — must match exactly for all sessions

Cross-file session recovery: emit_stress_session(seed=Y, n_sessions=10, n_files=6), run reassembler.py --merge on the directory, compare all sessions — each session's query list must match ground truth
Out-of-order fragment handling: emitter generates logs with reorder_window-magnitude out-of-order delivery; reassembler must still produce correct order
Continuation_dup deduplication: verify that sessions spanning file boundaries have exactly the correct number of queries (not one extra per boundary crossing)

SessionReassembler import and API: from reassembler import SessionReassembler; sr = SessionReassembler([path1, path2, ...]); assert all session_ids present; assert each session's queries match ground truth
replay_validator.py output: sessions appear in global_seq order; each session has correct header comment; queries are valid SQL byte strings (non-empty, no null bytes)
reorder_window from config: modify proxy_config.ini to reorder_window=3 vs reorder_window=12 and verify behavior is consistent with the configured value

verifier_knob.name: n_stress_seeds
verifier_knob.effect: Raising seeds/sessions/files increases the probability that all three bug classes (cross-file, dedup, reorder) are exercised and that partial fixes are caught; lowering to 1 seed with 1 file makes it trivially passable by sorting alone

expected_failure_modes: Solver sorts by frag_seq within each file but never implements cross-file session merging — passes single-file tests, fails cross-file tests
Solver implements cross-file merging but doesn't read fragment_format.md carefully enough to find the continuation_dup flag semantics — produces double query at every file boundary
Solver implements SessionReassembler but doesn't read proxy_config.ini for reorder_window — hardcodes a value that works on the sample but fails stress tests
Solver implements the class correctly but replay_validator.py session ordering is wrong (orders by session_id instead of first global_seq) — validator output fails ordering test
Solver relies only on the /app/tests/ samples to validate, never runs the emitter against the /var/log/pgproxy pre-generated logs to observe cross-file failures, and submits a partial fix
